rendered:
The sentence in question reads: Sun et al. integrated precursor biosynthesis genes (proC, serC, metH) into the cpxR locus, simultaneously enhancing precursor supply and relieving CpxR-mediated repression of the pig cluster; the engineered strain PG yielded 5.83 g L^(cid:0) 1 prodigiosin[1] with the citation[2] [101,117][3].

The matching entry in[4] Table 2[5] is the second prodigiosin row, whose strategy is[6] Integration of proC, serC, and metH to enhance precursor supply[7], cultivated in[8] shake flask[9] for 96[10] h, citing the same reference [101][11]. Its titer is given in mg per litre as 5830[12], i.e. 5.83[13] g/L, numerically identical to the value quoted in the running text.

The strain names, however, do not match. The text calls the engineered strain simply PG[14], whereas the table designates the same construct by parent and derivative as JNB5–1 → SMCH[15]; the designation used in the table appears nowhere else in the document, and the text never links it to the name it uses.[16] Note also that the name in the text is a near-duplicate of the strain named in the following sentence,[17] PG-6[18], which is itself a distinct table row[19] JNB5–1 → PG-6[20] with a different titer (10,250[21] mg/L) and reference [14][22]. So the correspondence rests on the strategy, cultivation time, titer and reference, not on the strain label, which is inconsistent between text and table.
